text:
marta: Quick thread: we need an approach for smooth automated reversion that minimizes cache churn and avoids flip-flop when doing A/B ramps. Goal: automatic, conservative, and observable.
pranav: Agreed. I think we should treat revert decisions as coming from a single "decision-aggregator" service that ingests prioritized signals (errors, latency, eval-drop, infra pressure). No ad-hoc votes from routers.
sam: +1. Operationally that aggregator should expose both a binary 'revert now' flag and a graded "health score" [0..1] so controllers can choose a soft vs hard path.
jen: Soft vs hard path = important. Hard = immediate 100% cut (use sparingly). Soft = ramp-down schedule based on current ramp stage and cache-warmth.
emily: Cache-warmth? love that. We should track a per-variant "cache_warmth" metric (0..100) derived from KV hit rates + recent prefix reuse. Low warmth => prefer slower ramp-down to avoid cold-miss latency spikes.
marta: Good. Also add an oscillation dampener: require a hysteresis counter that must exceed N before rolling forward again after a revert. Prevents re-ramp loops.
pranav: Agreed. Also consider a simulated-annealing style ramp: start at target, if health dips slightly, step back to previous stage; if worse, step back faster. This gives adaptive granularity.
sam: Nice. For modes, propose controller supports: "soft_rewind" (decrement to previous step), "staged_rewind" (decrement by fixed fraction), and "hard_rewind" (instant revert). Implement soft_rewind first.
jen: UI needs an override and a visual "replayable window" so SRE can mark a revert as intentional and bypass auto-recover for a period.
emily: For signals, rank them: 1) infra_critical (OOMs, queue_exhaust), 2) error_spike (5xx), 3) eval_drift (LLM score), 4) latency_guard (p95). infra_critical and error_spike should be able to force hard_rewind. others map to soft paths.
rollout-bot: schema-check: note that rollout-controller v3 will add new enums for rewind_mode and a cache_warmth gauge. Bump required.
pranav: Putting a short config sketch here (proto-like): ```json
{
  "variant": "v3-experiment",
  "target": 0.25,
  "ramp_schedule": [0.1,0.25],
  "rewind_policy": {
    "modes": ["soft_rewind","staged_rewind","hard_rewind"],
    "warmth_threshold": 30,
    "hysteresis_count": 3,
    "cooldown_s": 900,
    "oscillation_backoff_factor": 2
  },
  "signals": {
    "infra_critical": {"threshold": 0.01, "window_s": 60, "priority": "p1"},
    "error_spike": {"threshold": 0.05, "window_s": 30, "priority": "p1"},
    "eval_drift": {"threshold": 0.03, "window_s": 300, "priority": "p2"},
    "latency_p95": {"threshold_ms": 1200, "window_s": 60, "priority": "p2"}
  }
}
```
sam: Add a per-variant "max_auto_recover_attempts" to avoid continuous retries after repeated failures. Also emit an audit event with full signal payload whenever an automatic rewind happens.
jen: For console UX: add a slider for aggressiveness (conservative / balanced / aggressive) which maps to hysteresis_count and cool-down. And add a forced-rewind button with reason required.
emily: Observability: one composite metric "rollout_health_score" (0..1) and a single state metric "rollout_state" with values: ramping, steady, degrading, rewinding, blocked. Dashboards should show signals stacked for quick triage.
marta: Nice set. Two more infra notes: 1) controller must publish planned traffic deltas before applying them so routers can prefetch or flush caches incrementally; 2) when hard_rewind happens, tag replayable requests with header X-Replay-Friendly: true for TTL so caches can reconcile.
pranav: Implementation plan: decision-aggregator service (reads telemetry + infra events) -> outputs health score + recommended_rewind_mode -> rollout-controller v3 executes delta with chosen rewind_mode and publishes audit.
sam: I'll prototype soft_rewind in controller and add a simulation harness to validate annealing parameters.
jen: I'll mock console mappings for aggressiveness and forced controls.
emily: I'll define cache_warmth calculation and dashboard panels.
marta: I'll open a tracking ticket linking the above and schedule a 30m follow-up to agree on defaults. Meeting tomorrow 11:00. Anything blocking?
pranav: none from me.
sam: no blockers. I'll share sim results in the ticket. :rocket:
